name: GO Classes | IIITH PGEE 2025 Mock Test 7

question.text:
The table below shows the ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs that were used to represent different numbers.


For example, the number 32 was represented by the hieroglyphs $\cap \cap \cap \|$. What number is represented by the following combination of hieroglyphs?


  1. 1,423
  2. 10,423
  3. 14,023
  4. 14,203

When Yunji added all the integers from 1 to 9 , she mistakenly left out a number. Her sum turned out to be a square number. What number did Yunji leave out?
  1. 6
  2. 7
  3. 8
  4. 9

In the land of Markovia, there are three cities: $A, B$, and $C$. There are 100 people who live in $A, 120$ who live in $B$, and 160 who live in $C$. Everyone works in one of the three cities, and a person may work in the same city where they live. In the figure below, an arrow pointing from one city to another is labeled with the fraction of people living in the first city who work in the second city. (For example, $\frac{1}{4}$ of the people who live in $A$ work in $B$.) How many people work in $A$ ?

  1. 55
  2. 60
  3. 85
  4. 115

A number $N$ is inserted into the list $2,6,7,7,28$. The mean is now twice as great as the median. What is $N$ ?
  1. 14
  2. 20
  3. 28
  4. 34

A roll of tape is 4 inches in diameter and is wrapped around a ring that is 2 inches in diameter. A cross section of the tape is shown in the figure below. The tape is 0.015 inches thick. If the tape is completely unrolled, approximately how long would it be? Round your answer to the nearest 100 inches.

  1. 300
  2. 600
  3. 1200
  4. 1500

Two towns, $A$ and $B$, are connected by a straight road, 15 miles long. Traveling from town $A$ to town $B$, the speed limit changes every 5 miles: from 25 to 40 to 20 miles per hour ( mph ). Two cars, one at town $A$ and one at town $B$, start moving toward each other at the same time. They drive at exactly the speed limit in each portion of the road. How far from town $A$, in miles, will the two cars meet?
  1. 7.75
  2. 8
  3. 8.25
  4. 8.5

A batch of widgets costs $p+15$ dollars for a company to produce and each batch sells for $p(9-p)$ dollars. For which of the following values of $p$ does the company make a profit?
  1. 3
  2. 4
  3. 5
  4. 6

All the marbles in Maria's collection are red, green, or blue. Maria has half as many red marbles as green marbles and twice as many blue marbles as green marbles. Which of the following could be the total number of marbles in Maria's collection?
  1. 25
  2. 26
  3. 27
  4. 28

On the most recent exam on Prof. Xochi's class,
5 students earned a score of at least $95 \%$,
13 students earned a score of at least $90 \%$,
27 students earned a score of at least $85 \%$,
50 students earned a score of at least $80 \%$.
How many students earned a score of at least $80 \%$ and less than $90 \%$ ?
  1. 8
  2. 14
  3. 22
  4. 37

Rohan scored twice as many marks in English as he did in Science. His total marks in English, Science, and Mathematics are 126. If the ratio of his marks in English and Mathematics is $2: 3$, and his marks in English are:
  1. 63
  2. 20
  3. 21
  4. 42

A group of frogs (called an army) is living in a tree. A frog turns green when in the shade and turns yellow when in the sun. Initially, the ratio of green to yellow frogs was $3: 1$. Then 3 green frogs moved to the sunny side and 5 yellow frogs moved to the shady side. Now the ratio is $4: 1$. What is the difference between the number of green frogs and the number of yellow frogs now?

  1. 12
  2. 16
  3. 20
  4. 24

A cricket randomly hops between 4 leaves, on each turn hopping to one of the other 3 leaves with equal probability. After 4 hops, what is the probability that the cricket has returned to the leaf where it started?


  1. $\frac{19}{80}$
  2. $\frac{20}{81}$
  3. $\frac{1}{4}$
  4. $\frac{7}{27}$

Three Statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II, and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some bottles are towels. No towel is a pillow. All bottles are coats.
Conclusions:
  1. Some coats are towels.
  2. No coat is a towel.
  3. Some bottles are pillows.

  1. Only conclusion II follows.
  2. Both conclusions I and III follows.
  3. Only either conclusion I or II follows.
  4. Only conclusion I follows.

A bus takes 2 minutes to drive from one stop to the next, and waits 1 minute at each stop to let passengers board. Zia takes 5 minutes to walk from one bus stop to the next. As Zia reaches a bus stop, if the bus is at the previous stop or has already left the previous stop, then she will wait for the bus. Otherwise she will start walking toward the next stop. Suppose the bus and Zia start at the same time toward the library, with the bus 3 stops behind. After how many minutes will Zia board the bus?

  1. 17
  2. 19
  3. 20
  4. 21

Buzz Bunny is hopping up and down a set of stairs, one step at a time. In how many ways can Buzz Bunny start on the ground, make a sequence of 6 hops, and end up back on the ground? (For example, one sequence of hops is up-up-down-down-up-down.)


 

  1. 4
  2. 5
  3. 6
  4. 8

In a certain code language, 'TECHNOLOGY' is written as 'NHCETOLOGY', 'GENERATION' is written as 'RENEGATION'.
How will 'APOCALYPSE' be written in that language?
  1. AOCPALYPSE
  2. ACPOALYPSE
  3. ACOAPLYPSE
  4. ACOPALYPSE

If $L \times M$ means that $L$ is the mother of $M, L+M$ means that $L$ is the father of $M, L \div M$ means that $L$ is the sister of $M$. Then which of the following expression shows that $P$ is the father of $R$ ?
  1. $P+Q \div R$
  2. $P \div R+Q$
  3. $Q+P \div R$
  4. $P+Q \times R$

The number $x$ in the lower left corner is larger than the other three missing numbers. What is the smallest possible value of $x$ ?
 

-295
  -1
x 8

  2. 5

The areas of the two rectangles in the diagram are $25 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$ and $13 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$ as indicated.



What is the value of $x$ ?

  1. 3
  2. 4
  3. 5
  4. 6

The circle shown below on the left has a radius of 1 unit. The region between the circle and the inscribed square is shaded. In the circle shown on the right, one quarter of the region between the circle and the inscribed square is shaded. The shaded regions in the two circles have the same area. What is the radius $R$, in units, of the circle on the right?

  1. $\sqrt{2}$
  2. 2
  3. $2 \sqrt{2}$
  4. 4

Sekou writes the numbers $15,16,17,18,19$. After he erases one of his numbers, the sum of the remaining four numbers is a multiple of 4. Which number did he erase?
  1. 15
  2. 16
  3. 17
  4. 18

According to the chart, which two-month period had the greatest increase in electric energy cost?

  1. Between January and February
  2. Between May and June
  3. Between June and July
  4. Between July and August

Betty drives a truck to deliver packages in a neighborhood whose street map is shown below. Betty starts at the factory (labled $F$ ) and drives to location $A$, then $B$, then $C$, before returning to $F$. What is the shortest distance, in blocks, she can drive to complete the route?

  1. 20
  2. 22
  3. 24
  4. 26

In the following question, select the missing number from the given series. $5103,1701,567, ?, 63,21$
  1. 265
  2. 169
  3. 189
  4. 170

Jordan owns 15 pairs of sneakers. Three fifths of the pairs are red and the rest are white. Two thirds of the pairs are high-top and the rest are low-top. The red high-top sneakers make up a fraction of the collection. What is the least possible value of this fraction?
  1. 0
  2. $\frac{1}{5}$
  3. $\frac{4}{15}$
  4. $\frac{1}{3}$

Three-fourths of a consignment was sold at a profit of $8 \%$ and the rest at a loss of $4 \%$. If there was an overall profit of Rs.600, then find the value of the consignment.
  1. Rs. 15,000
  2. Rs.6,000
  3. Rs. 18,000
  4. Rs. 12,000

On Monday, Taye has $\$ 2$. Every day, he either gains $\$ 3$ or doubles the amount of money he had on the previous day. How many different dollar amounts could Taye have on Thursday, 3 days later?
  1. 3
  2. 4
  3. 5
  4. 6

Any three vertices of the cube $P Q R S T U V W$, shown in the figure below, can be connected to form a triangle. (For example, vertices $P, Q$, and $R$ can be connected to form isosceles $\triangle P Q R$.) How many of these triangles are equilateral and contain $P$ as a vertex?


 

  1. 0
  2. 1
  3. 2
  4. 3

Which combination of household sizes accounts for more than $50 \%$ of all owner-occupied housing units?
  1. 2- and 3-person
  2. 3- and 4-person
  3. 4- and 5-person
  4. 5- and 6-person

What percent of owner-occupied housing units are households with fewer than 4 people?

  1. $11.1 \%$
  2. $14.5 \%$
  3. $25.6 \%$
  4. $74.4 \%$

What is the value of
$$
\frac{1}{3} \cdot \frac{2}{4} \cdot \frac{3}{5} \cdots \frac{18}{20} \cdot \frac{19}{21} \cdot \frac{20}{22} ?
$$
  1. $\frac{1}{462}$
  2. $\frac{1}{231}$
  3. $\frac{1}{132}$
  4. $\frac{2}{213}$

Aaliyah rolls two standard 6-sided dice. She notices that the product of the two numbers rolled is a multiple of 6 . Which of the following integers cannot be the sum of the two numbers?
  1. 5
  2. 6
  3. 7
  4. 8

Approximately what was the average (arithmetic mean) electric energy cost per month for the first half of the year?

  1. $\$ 45$
  2. $\$ 50$
  3. $\$ 60$
  4. $\$ 70$

Henri Matisse's The Ochre Head represents the artist's exuberant display of his new mastery of a technique once peculiar to Picasso. Matisse has learned to artfully separate
color and drawing. The painting depicts a head and shoulders, a bouquet of red flowers in a dark
blue vase sitting upon a bench, a framed drawing of a woman's head, and an unframed painting
5 or drawing, also of a woman. But what is most striking about the painting is the way Matisse has
begun to allow his colors and his forms to play freely, even while they are coordinated. The ochre
of the head runs out past the form. Bits of blue from the bench appear in the man's neckline
or along his shoulder. The colors of the various frames and surfaces of the drawing on the wall
overlap and refuse to be constrained by definite lines of form. Although this technique is not given
10 the kind of free reign Picasso allows it in his Cubist period or in works such as Minotaur, it is still a stunning development for Matisse. And he seems aware of this fact. The painting's composition references Picasso's Still Life with Ancient Head from 1925, signaling Matisse's awareness that he is borrowing from his younger colleague.
According to the passage, all of the following are true of The Ochre Head EXCEPT:
  1. The artist avoided the constraint of coloring only between the lines.
  2. Its arrangement is similar to that of a piece by Picasso.
  3. It is considered among the best of Matisse's work.
  4. Its use of technique is more constrained than that of Minotaur.

In which month was the electric energy cost per Fahrenheit degree $\left({ }^{\circ} \mathrm{F}\right)$ of average temperature the least?

  1. April
  2. May
  3. October
  4. November

In January 1980 the Moana Loa Observation recorded carbon dioxide $\left(\mathrm{CO}_{2}\right)$ levels of 338 ppm (parts per million). Over the years the average $\mathrm{CO}_{2}$ reading has increased by about 1.515 ppm each year. What is the expected $\mathrm{CO}_{2}$ level in ppm in January 2030? Round your answer to the nearest integer.
  1. 399
  2. 414
  3. 420
  4. 444

Homo economicus, or economic human, denotes the idea of human beings as rational, narrowly self-interested agents who, given total information about opportunities and possible constraints, seek to obtain the highest possible well-being for themselves at the least possible cost. In the late 19th century, a host of economists built mathematical models based on the 5 conception of real humans as Homo economicus. Exponents of Homo economicus tend to acknowledge that total information is not possible in the real world; thus, breakdown in models based on the concept are due to imperfect information held by the self-interested economic actors. Amartya Sen has pointed out that Homo economicus ignores that people can and do commit to courses of action out of morality, 0 cultural expectations, and so forth. Veblen and Keynes allege that Homo economicus assumes far too great an understanding of macroeconomics on the part of humans. Tversky puts forth that  investors are not rational: they are unconcerned by small chances of large losses, but quite risk-averse regarding small losses. Bruno Frey points out that humans are often intrinsically motivated, and that such motivation explains heroism, craftsmanship, and other drives that do not fit neatly 5 into the model of a narrowly focused gain-seeker. Critics of the psychoanalytic tradition point out, somewhat obviously, that humans are frequently conflicted, lazy, and inconsistent.

Which of the following best describes the main idea of the passage?
  1. Homo economicus is a useful, if theoretical, actor to use in the formation of mathematical models.
  2. Homo economicus is a fundamentally flawed and thus theoretically useless construction, for a host of reasons.
  3. Homo economicus is often criticized by those who don't fully understand its function in economic theory.
  4. Homo economicus is a problematic construction, because it simplifies human motivations and is overly optimistic about human understanding.

According to the chart, in which two-month period did electric energy cost increase the least?

  1. Between January and February
  2. Between April and May
  3. Between May and June
  4. Between June and July

Anna and Bella are celebrating their birthdays together. Five years ago, when Bella turned 6 years old, she received a newborn kitten as a birthday present. Today the sum of the ages of the two children and the kitten is 30 years. How many years older than Bella is Anna?
  1. 1
  2. 2
  3. 3
  4. 4

Based on the total number of people living in all such households, which of the following is a correct ordering, from least to greatest, of 1-person households, 3-person households, and 5-person households?

  1. 1-person households, 3-person households, 5-person households
  2. 1-person households, 5-person households, 3-person households
  3. 3-person households, 1-person households, 5-person households
  4. 3-person households, 5-person households, 1-person households

Among the owner-occupied housing units represented in the chart above, approximately how many households are 5-person households?
 

  1. 2 million
  2. 3 million
  3. 4 million
  4. 5 million

Sarika, Dev, and Rajiv are sharing a large block of cheese. They take turns cutting off half of what remains and eating it: first Sarika eats half of the cheese, then Dev eats half of the remaining half, then Rajiv eats half of what remains, then back to Sarika, and so on. They stop when the cheese is too small to see. About what fraction of the original block of cheese does Sarika eat in total?
  1. $\frac{4}{7}$
  2. $\frac{3}{5}$
  3. $\frac{2}{3}$
  4. $\frac{3}{4}$

A person lent Rs. 23000 to $B$ for 3 years and Rs. 19000 to $C$ for 4 years on simple interest at the same rate of interest and received Rs. 3625 in all from both of them as interest. What is the annual rate of interest?
  1. 1.5 percent
  2. 3 percent
  3. 2.5 percent
  4. 4 percent

From point H, at 6: 30 pm , a train starts moving towards point K at the speed of $90 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{hr}$. Another train starts moving from point K at 7: $30 \mathrm{p} . \mathrm{m}$. towards point H at the speed of $72 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{hr}$. Both trains meet at 11:30 p.m. at point J . What is the ratio of the distance between HJ and KJ ?
  1. $25: 16$
  2. $5: 16$
  3. $36: 25$
  4. $31: 19$

Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains a grammatical error. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer. I am having trouble / deciding in / a gift for them. / no error
  1. a gift for them.
  2. No error
  3. I am having trouble
  4. deciding in

The coordinates of $\triangle A B C$ are $A(5,7), B(11,7)$, and $C(3, y)$, with $y>7$. The area of $\triangle A B C$ is 12. What is the value of $y$ ?


 

  1. 8
  2. 9
  3. 10
  4. 11

 Which of the following phenomena would exemplify Bruno Frey's critique of Homo economicus?
  1.  A woodworker spends months on the delicate inlay of a door, knowing that his many hours of hard work will inevitably
    result in a higher price when he comes to sell the piece.

  3.  An economist dedicates her career to illustrating a fundamental flaw in a particular theory, though she knows there will be no tangible reward for her efforts.
  4. None of them exemplify bruno frey's crtitique of homo economicus.

Buffalo Shuffle-o is a card game in which all the cards are distributed evenly among all players at the start of the game. When Annika and 3 of her friends play Buffalo Shuffle-o, each player is dealt 15 cards. Suppose 2 more friends join the next game. How many cards will be dealt to each player?
  1. 8
  2. 9
  3. 10
  4. 11

Let $f$ be a function from a set $X$ to a set $Y$. Consider the following statements.

  • $P$ : For each $x \in X$, there exists $y \in Y$ such that $f(x)=y$.
  • $Q$ : For each $y \in Y$, there exists $x \in X$ such that $f(x)=y$.
  • $R$ : There exist $x_1, x_2 \in X$ such that $x_1 \neq x_2$ and $f\left(x_1\right)=f\left(x_2\right)$.

The negation of the statement " $f$ is one-to-one and onto $Y$ " is

  1. $P$ or not $R$
  2. $R$ or not $P$
  3. $R$ or not $Q$
  4. $P$ and not $R$

In a recent NASA discovery, the planet Mars has three-handed philosophers. Consider a table with five three-handed philosophers and a pile of N chopsticks in the middle of the table. Each philosopher needs 3 chopsticks to eat. What is the smallest $N$ such that deadlock is impossible?

An upper-layer packet is split into $10$ frames, each of which has an $80$ percent chance of arriving undamaged. If no error control is done by the data link protocol, how many times must the message be sent on average to get the entire thing through?

  1. $7.4$
  2. $9.3$
  3. $6.7$
  4. $2.4$

Consider the virtual page reference string

$$\text{1, 2, 3, 2, 4, 1, 3, 2, 4, 1}$$

on a demand paged virtual memory system running on a computer system that has main memory size of $3$ page frames which are initially empty. Let $\text{LRU}$, $\text{FIFO}$ and $\text{OPTIMAL}$ denote the number of page faults under the corresponding page replacement policy. Then

  1. $\text{OPTIMAL} < \text{LRU} < \text{FIFO}$
  2. $\text{OPTIMAL} < \text{FIFO} < \text{LRU}$
  3. $\text{OPTIMAL} = \text{LRU}$
  4. $\text{OPTIMAL} = \text{FIFO}$

Given the following piece of code:

main(int argc, char ** argv)
{
    int child = fork();
    int c = 5;
    if(child == 0)
    {
        c += 5;
    }
    else
    {
        child = fork();
        c += 10;
        if(child)
            c += 5;
    }
}

How many different copies of the variable $\textsf{c}$ are there?

The process state transition diagram in the below figure is representative of

  1. a batch operating system

  2. an operating system with a preemptive scheduler

  3. an operating system with a non-preemptive scheduler

  4. a uni-programmed operating system

$$\begin{array}{ccll}\text { Job } & \begin{array}{c}\text { Service Time } \\ \text { (sec.) }\end{array} & \text { Arrival time } \\\hline 1 & 2 & t_0 \\ 2 & 5 & t_0 \\ 3 & 1 & t_0+1 \;\mathrm{sec} . \\ 4 & 9  & t_0+5\; \mathrm{sec} . \\ 5 & 3 & t_0+10 \;\mathrm{sec} . \\ 6 & 2 & t_0+15\; \mathrm{sec} .\end{array}$$
If a first-come-first-served scheduling algorithm is assumed, where ties are resolved in favor of the smaller numbered job, what is the average (arithmetic mean) number of seconds that a job waits before being assigned to the processor?

  1. $20 / 6$
  2. $21 / 6$
  3. $23 / 6$
  4. $31 / 6$

Consider the function $f(N)=\displaystyle{}\sum_{i=0}^{N} \sum_{j=0}^{i} j$

Which of the following is true about $f(N)?$

Consider a $1 \mathrm{~Mbps}$ satellite channel with $50 \mathrm{~ms}$ round trip propagation delay. We want to send a $1000$ bit frame, and we will not send a second frame until we receive acknowledgment for the first frame.

What fraction of the available bandwidth are we using?

  1. $1 / 40$
  2. $1 / 51$
  3. $1 / 2$
  4. $1 / 5$

Let $s$ be a sorted array of $n$ integers. Let $t(n)$ denote the time taken for the most efficient algorithm to determine if there are two elements with sum less than $1000$ in $s.$

Which of the following statements is true?

  1. $t(n)$ is $O(1)$
  2. $n < t(n) < n \log_{2} n$
  3. $n \log_{2} n < t(n) < \;^{n}\text{C}_{2}$
  4. $t(n) = \;^{n}\text{C}_{2}$

$\mathrm{X}_{1} \mathrm{X}_{0}=\mathrm{X}$ and $\text{Y}_{1} \text{Y}_{0}=\text{Y}$, where $\text{X}_{0}$ and $\text{Y}_{0}$ are the least significant bits. (A small circle on any line in a logic diagram indicates logical NOT.)

Which of the following always makes the output $\text{Z}$ have the value $1?$

  1. $\text{X}>\text{Y}$
  2. $\text{X}<\text{Y}$
  3. $\text{X} \neq \text{Y}$
  4. $\text{X} \geq \text{Y}$

$
\text { Let } A=\left(\begin{array}{ll}
4 & 1 \\
2 & 1
\end{array}\right) \text {. Find } A^{-1} \text {. }
$

  1. $ A^{-1}=\frac{1}{2}\left(\begin{array}{ll}
    1 & 1 \\
    2 & 4
    \end{array}\right)$
  2. $ A^{-1}=\frac{1}{-2}\left(\begin{array}{ll}
    1 & -1 \\
